title: Type 2 diabetes — WHO PEN baseline (draft)
summary: WHO/global baseline decision logic for type 2 diabetes diagnosis and primary-care management (WHO PEN / WHO diabetes guidance). Universal logic every country inherits until a national overlay (drug choices to the national EML, monitoring cadence) is authored. DRAFT — clinician verification required before approval.

criteria: Random plasma glucose >=11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) with symptoms.
HbA1c >=6.5% (48 mmol/mol) where assured testing is available.
diagnosis.note: Confirm with a repeat test on a separate day unless unequivocal hyperglycaemia with symptoms.

management: Lifestyle for all: diet, weight management, physical activity, tobacco cessation.
First-line pharmacotherapy: metformin, titrated as tolerated (caution/avoid in significant renal impairment).
Add a second agent (e.g. sulfonylurea) if target not met; insulin where indicated.
Cardiovascular risk management: BP control and statin per risk; foot care and annual screening.
targets: HbA1c <7% (53 mmol/mol) for most adults; individualise (relax in frailty/limited life expectancy).
Screen for retinopathy, nephropathy (urine albumin), and neuropathy.
redFlags: Ketones / heavy ketonuria, vomiting, drowsiness — assess for DKA and refer.
Very high glucose with dehydration in older patients — assess for hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state.
nationalOverlayNotes: Per-country overlays should map agents to the national Essential Medicines List and adopt national monitoring intervals.

references.label: WHO Package of Essential Noncommunicable (PEN) disease interventions for primary health care
